excerpt: Faster speech off signals for spec gen voice pipelines - KoljaB/RealtimeVAD
content_html:
Know that the speaker stopped, about 100 ms before Silero does.

RealtimeSTT · RealtimeTTS · Live demo · Spec · LiveKit plugin

A voice assistant can't do anything until it knows the user has stopped talking. Speech recognition, the LLM call and the voice output all wait for that one decision, and a normal voice activity detector takes a few hundred milliseconds to make it.

RealtimeVAD makes it sooner. It keeps Silero VAD to decide what is speech, and adds a second, faster check: every 10 ms it compares the audio level with the room's noise and with the speaker's own level. The moment the audio goes quiet, you get an event, long before Silero's probability has fallen.

  • Input: 16 kHz mono audio in chunks of any size (float32, int16 or int16 bytes).
  • Output: start, pause and end events, plus the audio of the running segment at any time.
  • Lead: speech-off a median 100 ms before Silero's probability drops, and 206 ms before Silero's VADIterator reports the end, on 3,279 real turns. The end itself comes before Silero's in 82 % of turns, by a median 70 ms.
  • Price: it also fires in short gaps between words, about ten times as often as Silero.
  • Quiet input: a quiet speaker's soft word endings are not silence; on a noisy quiet line the lead is gone instead (details).
  • Runs on: one CPU thread, far faster than realtime. Needs only numpy and onnxruntime; the Silero model is bundled, no torch.
  • Status: alpha (0.0.5). The API may still change.

Live demo

demo.mp4

The video uses a synthetic voice and shows a median lead of 92 ms. The 100 ms above is the median on real voice-assistant turns.

demo/ runs this page on your own microphone. It shows, turn by turn, how much sooner RealtimeVAD knew that you stopped than Silero alone, on the same audio.

Quick start

pip install realtimevad
from RealtimeVAD import VAD

vad = VAD()
for chunk in microphone_chunks():
    for event in vad.feed(chunk):
        if event.kind == "start":
            stream_to_asr(vad.audio())       # includes the audio just before speech began
        elif event.kind == "pause":
            speculate(vad.audio())           # the speaker may be done; this isn't the end yet
        elif event.kind == "end":
            finalize(event.segment.audio)

Events

Event Meaning When
start Speech has begun After about 64 ms of confident speech, so clicks don't trigger it. Speech Silero is never confident about (a short "mm-hmm", a quiet phone voice) starts after about 0.13 s at half confidence, if it is clearly louder than the room
pause The speaker may have stopped (speech-off) Within about 10 ms of the audio going quiet
end The segment is over 0.24 s after speech-off, unless speech resumes. Never later than Silero alone
onset Speech may have begun At the first confident frame, before start confirms it. Off by default: VAD(onset_events=True)

vad.audio() returns the running segment at any time, starting about 0.3 s before the speech. end carries the finished segment with its audio, start time, end time and the time the speech stopped.

If your assistant talks while the microphone is open, pass vad.feed(chunk, playback=True) for those chunks so its own voice is handled as possible echo. Every threshold and duration can be configured; SPEC.md lists what is guaranteed.

How to use pause

pause is early and often wrong, on purpose. It fires on every breath, every short gap between words and every stop consonant, so most pause events are followed by more speech.

  • Use it to start work you can cancel: finalize the transcript, call the LLM, prepare the voice output. Cancel when speech continues. A wrong pause then costs almost nothing, and a right one saves hundreds of milliseconds.
  • Never treat it as the end of the turn. Only end closes a segment.
  • Can't cancel quickly? Ignore pause and wait for end. The extra false alarms would cost you more than they save.

Already using Silero?

Change the import:

from silero_vad import load_silero_vad
from RealtimeVAD import VADIterator          # was: from silero_vad import VADIterator

vad_iterator = VADIterator(load_silero_vad(), sampling_rate=16000)
speech_dict = vad_iterator(chunk, return_seconds=True)   # {'start': ...} / {'end': ...} / None

The constructor and the results stay the same, but end arrives as soon as the audio goes quiet. Without a model argument, it uses the bundled Silero model and doesn't need torch.

Using LiveKit Agents?

livekit-plugins-realtimevad/ is a VAD plugin: realtimevad.VAD.load() in place of silero.VAD.load(). Its README shows how the events map and what it measured against the Silero plugin on the same audio. In short: against the Silero plugin's defaults the end of speech comes about 380 ms sooner, but most of that is the shorter silence setting (0.25 s instead of 0.55 s), which Silero can be given too. At the same setting RealtimeVAD's end is 65 to 110 ms earlier, and LiveKit's turn detector starts 95 to 180 ms earlier. Inside a LiveKit session the turn was committed about 150 ms sooner than with Silero's defaults and about 70 ms sooner than with Silero at 0.25 s.

Results

Measured on 3,279 turns from a live voice assistant, each with its trailing silence, with default settings. Silero's decisions are computed from the very same frame probabilities, so both see identical input. "Speech-off" is RealtimeVAD's last pause before the turn ended, against the first frame of Silero's final run below its threshold.

RealtimeVAD speech-off earlier than … median p25 – p75 p90 earlier in
Silero, probability below 0.5 (its default threshold) 100 ms 80 – 150 ms 214 ms 98 %
Silero, probability below 0.35 (VADIterator's end threshold) 110 ms 90 – 176 ms 230 ms 98 %
Silero VADIterator end, default 100 ms minimum silence 206 ms 186 – 272 ms 336 ms 99 %
Speech-off signals followed by more speech per second of speech turns without any
RealtimeVAD pause 1.5 17 %
Silero, probability below 0.5 0.14 86 %

Until 0.0.4 the first row read 110 ms. The 10 ms went into not cutting quiet speakers, see the next section.

The end event, against the end Silero's own silence count gives with the same thresholds and the same 0.24 s (2,323 turns where both closed the same segments inside the recording):

RealtimeVAD end earlier than Silero alone earlier in median p25 – p75 later in
0.0.5 82 % 70 ms 40 – 92 ms 0
the same without restarting the count after a click 51 % 18 ms 0 – 76 ms 0

Up to 0.0.4 a single loud 10 ms block inside the quiet after a word (a click, a lip smack, a breath) stopped the quiet count for good and left the end to Silero. That happened in a third of 680 sampled turns. The count now starts again after it.

Reproduce with your own recordings (16 kHz mono WAVs, one turn each, with trailing silence):

python benchmarks/speech_off_lead.py <wav dir> out.json

Quiet input and phone audio

Up to 0.0.4, "quiet" had a fixed floor (quiet_rms, about −54 dBFS). For a speaker around −32 dBFS that is fine. For a quiet one (a phone line recorded at source level, a distant microphone) the floor sits only a few dB under the speech, their soft word endings counted as silence, and 0.24 s later the segment ended while they were still talking. Since 0.0.5 the floor follows the speaker: it is quiet_rms or 20 dB below the speaker's own level, whichever is lower (floor_margin_db).

The same 3,401 turns, attenuated and sent through a simulated phone line (300–3400 Hz, 8 kHz, μ-law, line noise). "Ended while talking" counts turns with an end that the same detector does not make at the recorded level and that is followed by more speech. "Silero alone" is the same VAD with the quiet clock off, on the same audio.

Speech level Ended while talking: 0.0.4 0.0.5 Silero alone Lost ≥ 100 ms of speech: 0.0.4 0.0.5 Silero alone Speech-off lead 0.0.5
−32 dBFS (as recorded) – – – 0 0 0 100 ms
−38 dBFS 361 (11 %) 36 58 13 8 8 108 ms
−42 dBFS 609 (18 %) 37 97 26 10 10 116 ms
−52 dBFS 1,473 (43 %) 215 155 868 26 23 132 ms
−62 dBFS 1,832 (54 %) 269 303 1,778 419 415 124 ms
−47 dBFS in room noise at −62 dBFS 746 (22 %) 125 312 295 93 93 0 ms
phone line, −38 dBFS 285 416 391 266 234 229 112 ms
phone line, −48 dBFS 667 265 275 311 301 294 0 ms

What this says, and what it doesn't:

  • Quiet speakers are no longer cut. Ends while the speaker talks and lost speech are now where Silero alone has them. In all of these runs RealtimeVAD's last end was never later than Silero's.
  • A noisy quiet line has no lead. When the noise is less than about 20 dB below the speaker (the room-noise row, and the quiet phone line with its line noise), nothing can be called quiet without calling soft speech quiet. RealtimeVAD then ends where Silero does: correct, and no faster.
  • Very quiet and narrowband speech is a Silero limit. At −62 dBFS, and on the phone line, Silero itself is unsure. Speech it never scores 0.9 used to start no segment at all (476 of the phone-line turns, 1,264 at −62 dBFS). The soft start halves that (186 and 380); Silero at its own 0.5 threshold still hears more (139 and 353). More turns found also means more ends counted in the phone rows. Amplifying such input before the VAD helps Silero most.
  • Borderline endings. Ends with speech of the original recording inside the 0.24 s that counted as quiet are rarer than in 0.0.4 by a factor of 10 at −52 dBFS (1,970 turns then, 182 now), but restarting the count after a click added some back (141 without it). Ends followed by more speech and lost speech did not rise with it.
  • The phone path is simulated, and the reference for "still talking" is the original wideband recording. One speaker, one microphone.

What to set:

If … then
your input is quiet and clean nothing; the lead stays
you would rather keep the old fixed floor VAD(floor_margin_db=None)
soft starts open segments you don't want (background voices) VAD(soft_start_s=None)
you want Silero's own count only, no early end VAD(quiet_rms=0)
your input is quiet or a phone line, and clean try VAD(normalize_to_dbfs=-30), see below 
python benchmarks/quiet_input.py <wav dir> out.json

Amplifying quiet input for Silero (optional)

Silero is less sure about quiet speech, most of all on a phone line: it finds fewer turns and drops out inside them. VAD(normalize_to_dbfs=-30) amplifies the frames Silero sees, by up to 20 dB and never into clipping, until speech sits at −30 dBFS. Levels, the quiet clock and the audio you get back use the input as it came. Same turns as above:

Speech level No segment at all: off on Lost ≥ 100 ms of speech: off on
−32 dBFS (as recorded) 0 0 0 2
−52 dBFS 138 127 26 5
−62 dBFS 380 357 419 40
−47 dBFS in room noise 220 215 93 21
phone line, −38 dBFS 186 142 234 125
phone line, −48 dBFS 542 499 301 265
phone line, −58 dBFS 1,569 1,203 910 411

It is off by default because it is not free at normal level: 2 of 3,401 turns lost more than 100 ms, speech-off was earlier than Silero in 96 % instead of 98 % of turns, and in one phone-line turn the end came later than Silero alone. It needs Silero to score the speech 0.5 at least once before it acts, so the first quiet words of a stream can still be missed. On noisy quiet input the ends moved by more than the benchmark's "ended while talking" count can judge, so that count is not given here; borderline endings did not rise.

Short backchannels

"mm-hmm", "yeah", "okay": 200 real ones from meeting recordings (AMI corpus, close microphone, 0.15–0.8 s long). Up to 0.0.4, 50 of them were not reported as speech at all: Silero scored 35 between 0.5 and 0.9, below the start threshold, and 15 below 0.5. With the soft start 25 are missed, 15 of them Silero's own. A start comes a median 160 ms after the word begins. Whether such a sound is a backchannel, a turn or an interruption is not a VAD question and not answered here.

Limits

  • The numbers come from one speaker and one capture chain: browser capture with noise suppression and echo cancellation, mostly quiet rooms.
  • The lead needs audio that actually goes quiet after a word, and noise suppression helps that. In the 137 noisier turns (room level above −70 dBFS) the median lead was 102–124 ms. Without noise suppression in a loud room, expect less; with noise within about 20 dB of the speaker, none.
  • Earlier is not the same as correct: at the recorded level, whether a speech-off sometimes lands inside a soft word ending was not checked against word timings. The quiet-input table above checks it against the same audio at normal level.
  • The 100 ms are for speech-off. end waits 0.24 s after speech-off in both cases; its own gain over Silero is smaller (a median 70 ms, none in 18 % of turns) and depends on the noise.
  • Whisper is mostly not detected (Silero scores it below 0.5). Laughter, coughs and sneezes often are.
  • A DC offset in the input hides the silence from the quiet clock: no early end then, nothing lost.
  • 16 kHz mono only.

Development

pip install -e ".[dev]"
pytest

The edge-case tests in tests/audio/ run on about 100 MB of freely licensed audio that is not in git (speech in 8 languages, noise, music, coughs and laughter, whisper, real backchannels and hesitations). Without it they are skipped. To get it (about 1.3 GB of downloads, checked by sha256):

python tests/audio/fetch_audio.py
python tests/audio/fetch_backchannels.py
pytest tests/audio

They take about 10 s with 8 worker processes and print what each test guards, with the measured value and its limit. Sources and licenses: LICENSES-audio.md, LICENSES-backchannels.md.

License and credits

MIT. The bundled speech model is Silero VAD (MIT).

content_html_zh:
Know that the speaker stopped, about 100 ms before Silero does.

RealtimeSTT · RealtimeTTS · Live demo · Spec · LiveKit plugin

A voice assistant can't do anything until it knows the user has stopped talking. Speech recognition, the LLM call and the voice output all wait for that one decision, and a normal voice activity detector takes a few hundred milliseconds to make it.

RealtimeVAD makes it sooner. It keeps Silero VAD to decide what is speech, and adds a second, faster check: every 10 ms it compares the audio level with the room's noise and with the speaker's own level. The moment the audio goes quiet, you get an event, long before Silero's probability has fallen.

  • Input: 16 kHz mono audio in chunks of any size (float32, int16 or int16 bytes).
  • Output: start, pause and end events, plus the audio of the running segment at any time.
  • Lead: speech-off a median 100 ms before Silero's probability drops, and 206 ms before Silero's VADIterator reports the end, on 3,279 real turns. The end itself comes before Silero's in 82 % of turns, by a median 70 ms.
  • Price: it also fires in short gaps between words, about ten times as often as Silero.
  • Quiet input: a quiet speaker's soft word endings are not silence; on a noisy quiet line the lead is gone instead (details).
  • Runs on: one CPU thread, far faster than realtime. Needs only numpy and onnxruntime; the Silero model is bundled, no torch.
  • Status: alpha (0.0.5). The API may still change.

现场演示

demo.mp4

The video uses a synthetic voice and shows a median lead of 92 ms. The 100 ms above is the median on real voice-assistant turns.

demo/ runs this page on your own microphone. It shows, turn by turn, how much sooner RealtimeVAD knew that you stopped than Silero alone, on the same audio.

快速启动

pip install realtimevad
from RealtimeVAD import VAD

vad = VAD()
for chunk in microphone_chunks():
    for event in vad.feed(chunk):
        if event.kind == "start":
            stream_to_asr(vad.audio())       # includes the audio just before speech began
        elif event.kind == "pause":
            speculate(vad.audio())           # the speaker may be done; this isn't the end yet
        elif event.kind == "end":
            finalize(event.segment.audio)

活动

Event 意义 When
start Speech has begun After about 64 ms of confident speech, so clicks don't trigger it. Speech Silero is never confident about (a short "mm-hmm", a quiet phone voice) starts after about 0.13 s at half confidence, if it is clearly louder than the room
pause The speaker may have stopped (speech-off) Within about 10 ms of the audio going quiet
end The segment is over 0.24 s after speech-off, unless speech resumes. Never later than Silero alone
onset Speech may have begun At the first confident frame, before start confirms it. Off by default: VAD(onset_events=True)

vad.audio() returns the running segment at any time, starting about 0.3 s before the speech. end carries the finished segment with its audio, start time, end time and the time the speech stopped.

If your assistant talks while the microphone is open, pass vad.feed(chunk, playback=True) for those chunks so its own voice is handled as possible echo. Every threshold and duration can be configured; SPEC.md lists what is guaranteed.

How to use pause

pause is early and often wrong, on purpose. It fires on every breath, every short gap between words and every stop consonant, so most pause events are followed by more speech.

  • Use it to start work you can cancel: finalize the transcript, call the LLM, prepare the voice output. Cancel when speech continues. A wrong pause then costs almost nothing, and a right one saves hundreds of milliseconds.
  • Never treat it as the end of the turn. Only end closes a segment.
  • Can't cancel quickly? Ignore pause and wait for end. The extra false alarms would cost you more than they save.

Already using Silero?

Change the import:

from silero_vad import load_silero_vad
from RealtimeVAD import VADIterator          # was: from silero_vad import VADIterator

vad_iterator = VADIterator(load_silero_vad(), sampling_rate=16000)
speech_dict = vad_iterator(chunk, return_seconds=True)   # {'start': ...} / {'end': ...} / None

The constructor and the results stay the same, but end arrives as soon as the audio goes quiet. Without a model argument, it uses the bundled Silero model and doesn't need torch.

Using LiveKit Agents?

livekit-plugins-realtimevad/ is a VAD plugin: realtimevad.VAD.load() in place of silero.VAD.load(). Its README shows how the events map and what it measured against the Silero plugin on the same audio. In short: against the Silero plugin's defaults the end of speech comes about 380 ms sooner, but most of that is the shorter silence setting (0.25 s instead of 0.55 s), which Silero can be given too. At the same setting RealtimeVAD's end is 65 to 110 ms earlier, and LiveKit's turn detector starts 95 to 180 ms earlier. Inside a LiveKit session the turn was committed about 150 ms sooner than with Silero's defaults and about 70 ms sooner than with Silero at 0.25 s.

What this says, and what it doesn't:

  • Quiet speakers are no longer cut. Ends while the speaker talks and lost speech are now where Silero alone has them. In all of these runs RealtimeVAD's last end was never later than Silero's.
  • A noisy quiet line has no lead. When the noise is less than about 20 dB below the speaker (the room-noise row, and the quiet phone line with its line noise), nothing can be called quiet without calling soft speech quiet. RealtimeVAD then ends where Silero does: correct, and no faster.
  • Very quiet and narrowband speech is a Silero limit. At −62 dBFS, and on the phone line, Silero itself is unsure. Speech it never scores 0.9 used to start no segment at all (476 of the phone-line turns, 1,264 at −62 dBFS). The soft start halves that (186 and 380); Silero at its own 0.5 threshold still hears more (139 and 353). More turns found also means more ends counted in the phone rows. Amplifying such input before the VAD helps Silero most.
  • Borderline endings. Ends with speech of the original recording inside the 0.24 s that counted as quiet are rarer than in 0.0.4 by a factor of 10 at −52 dBFS (1,970 turns then, 182 now), but restarting the count after a click added some back (141 without it). Ends followed by more speech and lost speech did not rise with it.
  • The phone path is simulated, and the reference for "still talking" is the original wideband recording. One speaker, one microphone.

What to set:

If … then
your input is quiet and clean nothing; the lead stays
you would rather keep the old fixed floor VAD(floor_margin_db=None)
soft starts open segments you don't want (background voices) VAD(soft_start_s=None)
you want Silero's own count only, no early end VAD(quiet_rms=0)
your input is quiet or a phone line, and clean try VAD(normalize_to_dbfs=-30), see below 
python benchmarks/quiet_input.py <wav dir> out.json

Amplifying quiet input for Silero (optional)

Silero is less sure about quiet speech, most of all on a phone line: it finds fewer turns and drops out inside them. VAD(normalize_to_dbfs=-30) amplifies the frames Silero sees, by up to 20 dB and never into clipping, until speech sits at −30 dBFS. Levels, the quiet clock and the audio you get back use the input as it came. Same turns as above:

Speech level No segment at all: off on Lost ≥ 100 ms of speech: off on
−32 dBFS (as recorded) 0 0 0 2
−52 dBFS 138 127 26 5
−62 dBFS 380 357 419 40
−47 dBFS in room noise 220 215 93 21
phone line, −38 dBFS 186 142 234 125
phone line, −48 dBFS 542 499 301 265
phone line, −58 dBFS 1,569 1,203 910 411

It is off by default because it is not free at normal level: 2 of 3,401 turns lost more than 100 ms, speech-off was earlier than Silero in 96 % instead of 98 % of turns, and in one phone-line turn the end came later than Silero alone. It needs Silero to score the speech 0.5 at least once before it acts, so the first quiet words of a stream can still be missed. On noisy quiet input the ends moved by more than the benchmark's "ended while talking" count can judge, so that count is not given here; borderline endings did not rise.

Short backchannels

"mm-hmm", "yeah", "okay": 200 real ones from meeting recordings (AMI corpus, close microphone, 0.15–0.8 s long). Up to 0.0.4, 50 of them were not reported as speech at all: Silero scored 35 between 0.5 and 0.9, below the start threshold, and 15 below 0.5. With the soft start 25 are missed, 15 of them Silero's own. A start comes a median 160 ms after the word begins. Whether such a sound is a backchannel, a turn or an interruption is not a VAD question and not answered here.

限制

  • The numbers come from one speaker and one capture chain: browser capture with noise suppression and echo cancellation, mostly quiet rooms.
  • The lead needs audio that actually goes quiet after a word, and noise suppression helps that. In the 137 noisier turns (room level above −70 dBFS) the median lead was 102–124 ms. Without noise suppression in a loud room, expect less; with noise within about 20 dB of the speaker, none.
  • Earlier is not the same as correct: at the recorded level, whether a speech-off sometimes lands inside a soft word ending was not checked against word timings. The quiet-input table above checks it against the same audio at normal level.
  • The 100 ms are for speech-off. end waits 0.24 s after speech-off in both cases; its own gain over Silero is smaller (a median 70 ms, none in 18 % of turns) and depends on the noise.
  • Whisper is mostly not detected (Silero scores it below 0.5). Laughter, coughs and sneezes often are.
  • A DC offset in the input hides the silence from the quiet clock: no early end then, nothing lost.
  • 16 kHz mono only.

发展

pip install -e ".[dev]"
pytest

The edge-case tests in tests/audio/ run on about 100 MB of freely licensed audio that is not in git (speech in 8 languages, noise, music, coughs and laughter, whisper, real backchannels and hesitations). Without it they are skipped. To get it (about 1.3 GB of downloads, checked by sha256):

python tests/audio/fetch_audio.py
python tests/audio/fetch_backchannels.py
pytest tests/audio

They take about 10 s with 8 worker processes and print what each test guards, with the measured value and its limit. Sources and licenses: LICENSES-audio.md, LICENSES-backchannels.md.
